title: Two 1 mm gaps 15 mm apart (half a wavelength at 10 GHz) driven in phase: array pattern and active resistance
source: An array of Hertzian dipoles: the far field is the element's (∝ sin θ) times the array factor Σ Iₙ e^{jk r̂·rₙ}, its power ½ Σ Re(Z_mn I_n I_m*) with the exact mutual impedances; each gap's active resistance is R₁₁ + Re Z₁₂ for equal currents (C. A. Balanis, Antenna Theory, 4th ed., §6.2, §8.6; emcraft-theory radiation::gap_array_directivity, mutual_impedance_parallel)

quantities.quantity: directivity broadside to the pair, θ = 90°, φ = 90°
quantities.reason: six second-order elements per wavelength, a Huygens box 12.6 mm from the gaps (much closer, the gaps' singular near fields are too coarse on it): +0.7 %

quantities.quantity: directivity at θ = 45° in the pair's plane (φ = 0)
quantities.reason: a side lobe between the element's null and the array's: −2.9 %

quantities.quantity: directivity along the pair, θ = 90°, φ = 0 (the array factor's null)
quantities.reason: half a wavelength apart in phase cancel along their line: 5e-5
